key_insight: Agentic LLM systems are moving from lab demos to real-world products, and deployment success depends less on benchmark scores alone and more on robustness, safety, and reliability in messy environments. The paper reframes agent research around what it takes to make these systems work in production across domains like software engineering, science, and finance.
problem_solved: It addresses the gap between academic agent research and production deployment, where systems must operate safely, reliably, and consistently with tools, workflows, and other agents.
method: Synthesizes research and deployment lessons for agentic LLM systems.
Highlights practical challenges in real-world settings, including robustness, safety, and reliability.
Connects benchmark-driven innovation with operational requirements for production-scale agent deployments.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a deployment-oriented lens for building agents that can be trusted in real applications. It helps teams move beyond prototype performance toward systems that are resilient, governable, and usable at scale.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing an agent moving from planning to tool use to multi-agent coordination.
Split-screen comparison of research benchmarks vs. real-world deployment constraints.
Risk matrix or dashboard highlighting robustness, safety, and reliability.
Domain icons for software engineering, science, and finance to show application breadth.
paper_title: Agents in the Wild: Where Research Meets Deployment
paper_authors: Grace Hui Yang, Pranav N. Venkit, Hooman Sedghamiz, Enrico Santus, Victor Dibia
